minutes.headline: Task force agreed to hire consultant George for street-light LED project, under 10k, pending grant eligibility check.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force discussed an RFP and consultant scope for converting street lights to LED, including the audit, dimming and controls, and whether grant funds may pay a consultant. Members also discussed unreconciled lights with Unitil, the expected utility incentive, and a preliminary idea of solar on the landfill. No formal votes except adjournment; action items were set.

attendees.name_as_heard: George Woodbury (Right Smart / Light Smart Energy Consulting)

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; two attendees (Hannah, Abby) had none.
A high school senior attending for a civics class assignment said she had no questions.

budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant's audit portion was quoted at roughly a few thousand dollars, with the consulting portion about double.
Total proposal is under the threshold where formal bids are needed; best practice suggests two to three estimates.
Chair asked the grant administrator whether a small share of the LED grant could pay a consultant; the grant's budget language covers design and project oversight.
Installed cost estimated in a range with an expected incentive; unclear how incentive money would be received or appropriated.

budget_items.topic: Annual street light cost and savings
budget_items.what_was_said: Consultant said the town spends a certain amount per year on lights and savings could begin by January; a pilot would raise his cost.
Unitil bills Fitchburg for part of the rated output for dimmed lights; a programmable dimming module could be cheaper than monitored control.
A consulting firm for landfill solar would take a percentage of cost as a fee.

decisions.decision: Chair to clarify with the grant administrator that a consultant for implementation oversight is an eligible use of the grant.
Chair to work with Heather to confirm hiring the consultant meets best procurement practice and get him on board as soon as possible.
Chair to invite the select board chair to the next meeting to discuss the landfill solar and town energy program, and to move the RFP forward.
Members agreed to hand the expert-match technical assistance application (phase two deadline in November) to the select board chair to pursue.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed informally to hire a consultant for the street-light LED project, with the cost under the procurement threshold and subject to a grant-eligibility check.
The chair is to confirm with the grant administrator that paying a consultant for implementation oversight is an eligible use of the LED grant.
Members discussed the RFP scope, including the street-light audit, dimming and controls, and lights that Unitil's records do not reconcile.
Members discussed the expected Unitil incentive and noted it is unclear how that money would be received or appropriated.
The task force held no votes except adjournment. It referred landfill solar to the next meeting and handed the expert-match assistance application to the select board chair.

why_it_matters: Street lights are a recurring line in the town's electric bill, so how the LED conversion is overseen and paid for affects what residents pay for lighting.
If grant money cannot pay the consultant, the cost could fall on the town budget, and the incentive from Unitil still has no stated route into the town's accounts.
